dossier.overview:
Pokémon accessories are cosmetic layers on the summary portrait and optional overworld walk sprite: one equipped slot per Pokémon, drag placement in a dressing UI, and per-facing sprite rules (example: ribbon full width south, clipped east/west, hidden north).

Accessories and ribbons are Resort-earned (side quests, missions, guest gifts, Pokémon happiness gifts). The only cosmetics that travel in from cartridge data are held items (Dark Glasses, belts, etc.) projected as visuals when the item is legitimately on that Pokémon.

Entry point: mirror smart object in the accessory building beside the Glamping Tents on the Island Atlas.

sections.title: Pokémon accessories
sections.summary: Feature spec, rendering, ribbons, and reactive Pokémon / NPC observers. Generation reference assets are on the second tab.

blocks.body: Spark idea (not committed). Accessories echo contest decorations (Gen 4), photo stickers (Gen 5), and PSS props (Gen 6), but Resort owns every id, unlock, and equip state. Nothing from those systems is read off a save except held-item visuals.

blocks.html:
FieldSpecification
Equipped slotsOne accessory per Pokémon (summary layer + optional overworld layer)
InventoryMultiple copies of the same accessory id allowed; one active equip per Pokémon
RemovalPlayer may unequip at any time; disliked items may trigger a Pokémon-initiated removal prompt (see Reactions)
Cartridge importHeld items only (see Held-item projection). No contest accessories, photo stickers, PSS props, or ribbon bytes from saves
RibbonsResort-earned ribbon ids only; see Ribbons

Acquisition channelWhat unlocks
Side questsStory or location-tied accessory ids (one-time rewards)
MissionsRepeatable or dailies; includes ribbon-tier rewards after contest-style goals
Guest giftsNPC handoffs after affinity or event flags
Pokémon giftsRandom offer when happiness crosses a threshold (mechanic TBD: threshold curve, cooldown, Nature bias)
Held-item projectionNot unlocked: cosmetic appears when the held item is already on the Pokémon from cartridge / OpenHome

RuleSpecification
EligibilityPokémon currently holds a whitelisted item id from cartridge / OpenHome data
VisualHeldItemProjectionDef maps item id to accessory sprites (glasses, belt, scarf, etc.)

ExportProjection reads held item bytes only; Resort does not write new held items onto a save for cosmetics

blocks.title: Accessory visibility and reactions
blocks.caption: Equip change broadcasts to nearby actors; no stat changes from social barks
blocks.source:
flowchart TB
    EQ["Equip change on pkrid"] --> VIS["AccessoryVisibilityEvent"]
    VIS --> SELF["Equipped PokemonActor"]
    VIS --> NEAR["Nearby PokemonActor + TrainerNPC"]
    SELF --> PREF["NatureAffinity check"]
    PREF --> EM["Emote idle sparkle or removal prompt"]
    NEAR --> TAG["Contest tag + species bark table"]
    TAG --> DLG["Flavor dialogue or emote offer"]

blocks.html:
AccessoryDef fieldPurpose
contestTagsHidden coolness, beauty, cuteness, etc. (contest-stat alignment for affinity scoring)
natureAffinityPer-Nature like / neutral / dislike
speciesOverridesOptional per-species preference exceptions
observerBarksOptional lines for NPCs and overworld Pokémon when this accessory id is visible

Equipped Pokémon preferenceRuntime behavior
LikePositive idle or sparkle; optional dialogue line
NeutralNo extra line
DislikePokémon may request removal; player chooses allow or refuse
Refused removalOver time, dialogue set where the Pokémon adapts to the accessory

Integration with Overworld NPC AI: visible accessories are inputs to soft scoring, not hard filters. A guest Pokémon wearing a coolness-tagged hat may increase weight for emote offers toward other guests with matching contestTags. Trainer NPCs can use observerBarks when the player partner enters interaction range. Partner follower idle (separate idea) may add a Nature-weighted emote when the equipped accessory matches natureAffinity.

Reactions are flavor only: no battle stat changes, no friendship deltas from barks alone.
